mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a cross-team operation to succeed (opOutcome = Success) and even produce an audit entry. Both NoInformationLeakage and FR_011_FR_014_CrossTeamIsolation assert that cross-team operations must yield NotFound with no audit entry — without F_CrossTeamIsolation the solver can find a counterexample trivially.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamViolation { some op : Operation | some op.opTargetTask and op.opTargetTask.taskTeam != op.opCallerTeam and op.opOutcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows two distinct AuditEntry atoms to share the same (aeTask, aeActor, aeActorRole, aeChangeDesc, aeTeam) tuple, simulating an in-place overwrite. The AppendOnly and FR_016_AuditAppendOnly assertions check for exactly this uniqueness property and will find the counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2 : AuditEntry | ae1.aeTask = ae2.aeTask and ae1.aeActor = ae2.aeActor and ae1.aeActorRole = ae2.aeActorRole and ae1.aeChangeDesc = ae2.aeChangeDesc and ae1.aeTeam = ae2.aeTeam }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a non-owner MemberRole caller to get Success on PatchTask/DeleteTask against a task they don't own. Both OwnershipBasedAccess and FR_008_FR_009_FR_010_OwnerAdminAccess assert that such an attempt must yield PermDenied, not Success.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerCheckViolation { some op : Operation | op.opKind = PatchTask and op.opCallerRole = MemberRole and some op.opTargetTask and op.opTargetTask.taskTeam = op.opCallerTeam and op.opTargetTask.taskOwner != op.opCaller and op.opOutcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets the solver assign an opAuditEntry to an operation whose outcome is not Success (e.g., ValidationFail or PermDenied). AuditCompleteness asserts that only successful operations produce audit entries, and ValidationBeforeMutation specifically checks that validation failures leave no trace.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditOnFailureViolation { some op : Operation | op.opOutcome = ValidationFail and some op.opAuditEntry }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows an AuditEntry to record a different actor or role than the operation's actual caller and callerRole — a mis-attribution. Both AttributionCorrectness and FR_015_AuditEntryShape assert that aeActor = opCaller and aeActorRole = opCallerRole for every operation that produces an entry.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some op : Operation | some op.opAuditEntry and op.opAuditEntry.aeActor != op.opCaller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the permission-matrix body leaves PermMatrix.Allowed unconstrained. LeastPrivilege can then find a successful operation whose (callerRole, opKind) pair is absent from the matrix; PermissionCompleteness finds the cell count ≠ 12; PrivilegeMonotonicity finds an operation kind allowed for Member but not for Admin.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermMatrixViolation { not (AdminRole -> GetAudit) in PermMatrix.Allowed and (MemberRole -> GetAudit) in PermMatrix.Allowed }
